rule: Backup failure must prevent mutation of the protected object.
Write via temporary file, fsync, metadata preservation and atomic replace.
Concurrent mutating APPLY runs must fail closed; no user-invokable RESTORE run is part of the v3 contract.
Manifest writes must be atomic and durable enough to survive interruption.
Non-symmetric changes and warnings must be machine-visible.
Capture live values before applying managed sysctl changes.
Apply only the managed drop-in; never global sysctl --system.
Compensate recorded keys individually only inside failed uncommitted APPLY; partial/reboot cases require explicit external-recovery classification.
Capture package set before transactional installation.
Transaction-local compensation may act only on the package delta attributable to the current uncommitted APPLY.
Failed-uncommitted APPLY compensation must not purge packages that predated the transaction.
Historical donor contract only. Selecting a post-APPLY RESTORE manifest is excluded from v3; completed APPLY recovery is EXTERNAL_SNAPSHOT.
Transaction-local file compensation must use recorded backup/pre-state evidence rather than inferred prior state.
Executable architecture tests should compare documentation/contract with actual dispatch order.
Future APPLY must record enough pre-state and feature-state for audit and compensation of a failed uncommitted transaction; no completed-APPLY RESTORE contract is created.
Changes that cannot be transaction-locally compensated must be recorded explicitly with external-recovery classification, never inferred.

mechanism: never weaken an already stricter runtime value
rule: Apply must not lower a live value that is already stricter than the managed target.

mechanism: profile gating of every mutating action
rule: Each action declares the minimum profile that authorises it; lower profiles skip it explicitly.

mechanism: two-phase transaction for files created by apply
rule: A file created by apply is recorded as pending before creation and committed only after success.

mechanism: authentication lockout policy is multi-file and order sensitive
rule: Lockout policy spans conf and PAM stacks; partial application must fail closed.
